item.text: {"case_id":"SHC073","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C09","C10","C02"],"selected_candidate_label":"C09","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C09 plausibly supplied the concrete drafting template for nearly the entire operative monument portion of the child. Both proclamations use the same sequence: donated land and public-interest recitals; a proclamation adding specifically described land to a national monument subject to valid existing rights; a warning against damaging monument features or settling on its lands; and assignment of supervision, management, and control to the National Park Service under the same 1916 statute. C10 and C02 closely match the child's anomalous opening trademark recital, but that recital is only a fragment and does not match the child's operative machinery; C09 is therefore materially stronger
